title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) that measured whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The preregistered contract used shared_initial_generation (one initial model generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded conditions) to isolate repair-mediated differences from generator sampling variance. We ran 200 paired tasks (50 per prespecified stratum: IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step) with declared generator gpt-5-mini and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair attempt per task). All archived per-episode scoring artifacts show both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), yielding a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0, paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair_count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not empirically computable. We reconcile this degenerate null to the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract, provide a concise validator-rule summary and contamination-pointer with archived checks confirming no rule firings, quantify the zero-discordant outcome and its inferential consequences, present execution accounting and reproducibility pointers to archived artifacts, and discuss construct/internal/external validity implications and reproducible follow-ups.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent-to-configuration translation with large language models promises operational productivity but raises acute safety concerns: a single incorrect device command can trigger outages, violate policies, or create routing instability. A widely proposed mitigation is a generate→validate→repair workflow in which a deterministic verifier (sandbox) checks semantic/policy properties and either blocks or drives automated repair. Prior work proposes these patterns and component frameworks, but controlled quantification of a verifier’s marginal benefit—separating repair-mediated corrections from generator sampling variance—remains limited.

We preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 to answer the confirmatory question: does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors compared to LLM-only generation when the initial generation is shared between arms (shared_initial_generation)? Shared_initial_generation intentionally isolates repair-mediated differences: because the same initial candidate is evaluated under both conditions, any observed paired discordance must be due to repair activity. Our principal contributions are: (1) a sealed preregistered paired-trial design that enforces shared_initial_generation and a single primary estimand; (2) a completed, fully archived execution of 200 paired tasks balanced across four prespecified strata with deterministic per-episode validator traces; and (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation of a degenerate null outcome together with reproducible follow-ups that trade off generator variance, repair budget, and validator fidelity.
sections.related_work: Recent literature documents rapid adoption of LLMs and agentic patterns for NetOps tasks including intent-to-configuration translation, constrained configuration generation, and prototype remediation loops (Nguyen Tu et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2025; Mekrache & Ksentini, 2024). Multiple works propose generate→validate→repair or self-critique patterns as practical mitigations and integrate verifiers or toolchains in agentic workflows (Sang, 2025; Okula, 2026). Surveys and architecture papers emphasize that operational reliability depends on surrounding architecture (tool integration, audit traces, human gates) rather than model capability alone (Bilal et al., 2026; Malik, 2026), and separate studies present taxonomies of agentic failure modes and recommend layered defenses (Maharaj, 2026; Vadlamudi, 2026). Our experiment differs by preregistering a single primary estimand in a paired design, enforcing shared_initial_generation to attribute any observed effect specifically to repair, and fully archiving deterministic per-episode validator traces and reconciliation artifacts to support reproducible interpretation and exact diagnostics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered as CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 prior to execution (preregistration_sha256: aa4055d52c118741524c4c42d07efa977372be338b9bd96069dc7abfc5b32ac4). The primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rate (guarded − baseline); per-task outcome is binary: "validator-clean" (no violations reported on the final configuration) vs "validator-detected error" (one or more violations). Preregistered inferential test: exact McNemar two-sided test (α = 0.05). We report a paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI using 10,000 resamples with archived seed = 1729.

Sample, strata, and inclusion rules: The confirmatory sample is 200 distinct intent-to-configuration tasks in a paired design (200 tasks × 2 conditions = 400 episodes) balanced across four prespecified strata (50 per stratum). Tasks were deterministically generated and recorded in the authoritative task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b). No preregistered exclusions were triggered in the final run.

Shared_initial_generation contract and adapter implementation: To attribute differences specifically to repair, the preregistered contract produced one initial model generation per task and reused that candidate for both baseline and guarded evaluations (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1). Execution used a hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter that implements a bounded generate→validate→repair transformation with at most one repair attempt per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The declared generator in the archived execution configuration is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider accounting confirms model_calls_used = 200, matching the preregistered contract and the adapter's provider-call accounting in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json.

Deterministic validator semantics (harm-oracle) and concise rule summary: The primary validator is a deterministic Batfish-style verifier implemented in the experiment harness; per-episode validator traces record validation_before, validation_after, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, and violation_codes. The preregistered validator rule-classes implemented in the harness (human-readable summary) are:

- R1 — Reachability violation: required intra/inter-VLAN or intent-prescribed paths absent after candidate application.
- R2 — ACL/policy violation: contradictions of explicit intent-specified permit/deny constraints.
- R3 — Routing anomaly: loops, next-hop mismatches, or blackholes inconsistent with the intent.
- R4 — Interface/workflow invariant violation: make-before-break constraints, required shutdown/configure/restore sequences, group constraints (e.g., one-of-two uplinks must remain up).
- R5 — Dangerous-command flag: commands matched by a regex-based safety detector (forbidden operations).

These rule classes correspond to the harm-oracle used to form the binary primary outcome; mapping of rule IDs to human-readable descriptions is archived alongside per-episode traces in the execution bundle. Representative per-episode scoring traces that show the validator fields and empty violation_codes arrays include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256: b8ebf9546dabb93b06b15d40152e35a3e96a9d1c98cee131bb7f8065a8b6a2b4) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256: 020baed3e0e4283cc5e25413af002166998bfc587a1919046ca53dab09251b30). The full raw per-episode results and validator-related records are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: 9ec4eb2ce01f16d9eb0191b80eda199ec2655637aa2c6c775f8babb62962b46f), which provides machine-verifiable traces for every applied rule check.

Contamination checks: Automated contamination checks were executed as preregistered; their (empty) result is archived at analysis/contamination_summary.csv (sha256: 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222) and confirm no flagged items in the released task bank used here.

Analysis plan, missingness, and multiplicity: Primary confirmatory analysis follows the preregistered plan: exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes with paired-bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729). The preregistered missingness plan used a complete-pair policy. No technical failures occurred in execution (failed_episode_count = 0). Exploratory subgroup analyses by stratum are labeled exploratory and reported without multiplicity adjustment.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and artifacts: Execution completed the full preregistered 400 episodes (200 tasks × 2 conditions) with zero failed episodes and zero excluded pairs (execution started_at_utc = 2026-08-28T11:15:20.528566+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-08-28T11:37:01.389670+00:00). Provider accounting: model_calls_used = 200, cache_hit_count = 0; deterministic reconciliation confirms these counts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Representative reproducibility pointers: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b), execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: 9ec4eb2ce01f16d9eb0191b80eda199ec2655637aa2c6c775f8babb62962b46f), execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c), analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256: 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).

Primary paired outcomes and exact counts: Aggregated scoring artifacts show baseline validator-clean = 200/200 and guarded validator-clean = 200/200. The four-cell paired contingency table is n_11 = 200 (both-clean), n_10 = 0 (guarded-only-clean), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-clean), n_00 = 0 (both-error). The point estimate for the paired difference (guarded − baseline) is 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) yields 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. The canonical paired contingency artifact is analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c).

Discordant-pair quantification and inferential consequences: The executed dataset has zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0), a fact recorded in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256: 7bc1bd2a...). The preregistered power calculation assumed an appreciable discordant-pair proportion (p12+p21 ≈ 0.25), which did not hold here; with zero observed discordant pairs the McNemar test is uninformative and the bootstrap CI is degenerate. For scale interpretation, the smallest non-zero absolute paired difference that could be observed in this 200-pair design corresponds to a single discordant pair, i.e., 1/200 = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points); however power to detect such a minuscule effect is negligible under the original assumptions. The observed degenerate CI therefore reflects the deterministic outcome in the archived traces rather than a failure of the analysis pipeline.

Repair activity and secondary estimand: Because no validator-detected errors occurred for any shared initial candidate, the bounded repair policy was never invoked (repair_count = 0). Representative per-episode guarded traces confirm repair_applied = false and validation_after.violation_count = 0 (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256: 020baed3e0e4...). Therefore the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate—the fraction of initial-error tasks where final config is validator-clean) is not empirically computable from these data; this is explicitly reported here and in the Abstract and Conclusion.

Diagnostics, contamination, and reconciliation: Automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items; analysis/contamination_summary.csv (sha256: 389227f0d1e8...) is empty. Missingness summary shows complete_pairs = 200 and zero missing episodes. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and that all deterministic checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). These artifacts substantiate that the observed null result does not stem from execution loss or manifest mismatches.

Representative examples: The submitted bundle includes per-task JSON traces for every episode; representative examples showing validator.before/after snapshots and empty violation_codes include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256: b8ebf...), task-000002-baseline.json (sha256: c5ba3...), and task-000004-baseline.json (sha256: 2d39d6...). Each record includes normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and validator fields that practitioners can inspect.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation of the degenerate null: Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract and the supplied synthetic 200-task corpus, the declared generator produced validator-clean candidates for every task; the deterministic validator’s validation_after.violation_count was zero across episodes. This empirical fact explains the degenerate null: with no initial failures there was nothing for a bounded repair loop to correct under the preregistered adapter policy. The experiment therefore supports the conditional claim: "given a generator that produces validator-clean shared candidates on this synthetic task bank, a bounded validator/repair wrapper produces no measurable paired improvement." It does not answer the counterfactual of whether a repair loop would help when independent generation produces unsafe candidates, when repair budgets are larger, or when the validator semantics differ.

Design trade-offs and operational implications: Shared_initial_generation improves causal attribution (any discordance must come from repair) but reduces the probability of observing baseline failures. Practitioners and researchers should treat shared vs independent generation as answering distinct operational questions: (a) shared_initial_generation isolates repair effectiveness conditional on specific candidate-correction capability; (b) independent generation evaluates end-to-end production risk reduction when generation is stochastic. The archived bundle supports direct, reproducible follow-ups to cross this axis: (A) permit independent condition generation (two independent model calls per task) to increase baseline failure probability and enable repair opportunities; (B) increase repair budget or enable iterative/tool-assisted repair; (C) enrich the harm-oracle with vendor-specific semantics.

Statistical interpretation and degenerate CI: The observed paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] is degenerate because the contingency table has zero discordant pairs. This reflects a deterministic outcome in the archived artifact set, not a failure of the bootstrap procedure. In practice this result denotes that across the archived shared-initial candidates and deterministic validator semantics there was no observed room for repair to operate under the preregistered contract.

Construct and external validity cautions: The primary outcome depends on validator expressiveness and task-bank difficulty. Our synthetic task corpus encodes workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break patterns and allowed-touched-field sets) but remains a sandbox: the deterministic Batfish-style validator used here does not emulate every vendor-specific nuance or production telemetry source. The run used a single declared generator family (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair), so conclusions do not generalize across models or repair strategies. Additionally, shared_initial_generation reduces the probability that generation variance will expose repair utility; thus absence of observed benefit does not imply absence of benefit under independent-generation, model heterogeneity, or adversarial perturbations.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed preregistered paired trial to measure the marginal effect of a deterministic Batfish-style validator in a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline under a shared_initial_generation contract. For the synthetic 200-task bank and declared generator (gpt-5-mini), every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: both baseline and guarded arms were validator-clean on all tasks, giving an exact paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked, so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate >50%) is not estimable from these data. These artifact-grounded results do not refute the potential value of verifier-assisted workflows; rather they demonstrate that preregistered contract choices (shared vs independent generation), task-bank challenge level, validator fidelity, and repair policy jointly determine whether verifier assistance yields an observable benefit. The archived execution bundle contains all artifacts necessary to reproduce the run and to design follow-ups that trade off generator variance and repair opportunity to quantify repair-mediated gains in realistic settings.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-style sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single declared model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

The preregistered shared_initial_generation contract produced exactly one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduced the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
